threads_text: Apple's iOS 27.2 is out, and Siri AI can now recall your past conversations, so you can ask about something it told you days ago. It also reads more of your phone, from voicemails to photos in Messages, with a new setting to exclude apps. Would you want Siri to remember everything you ask it?
caption:
Apple released iOS 27.2 on October 26, and Siri AI can now recall your past conversations.
It also draws on more of your phone, like voicemails, Calendar attendees and photos sent in Messages.
A new Excluded Apps setting lets you choose what Siri can see. Siri AI needs an iPhone 15 Pro or newer.

Would you want Siri to remember everything you ask it?

paragraphs.text: Apple released iOS 27.2 and iPadOS 27.2 on Monday, October 26, 2026, according to MacRumors. They are the first major updates to iOS 27 and iPadOS 27, which arrived in September. The largest changes in the release are to Siri AI, Apple's assistant.

The most visible change is memory. Siri AI can now recall earlier conversations, so a user can ask a follow-up about something the assistant said before. Cult of Mac gave the example of a restaurant Siri recommended days earlier, which a user can now ask about again without repeating the original request.

The update also widens the personal information Siri can draw on. According to MacRumors and Beebom, Siri AI can now use photos attached in Messages, the attendees of Calendar events, voicemails, and improved results from Safari history and the Safari Reading List.

To balance that wider reach, Apple added a control called Excluded Apps. Cult of Mac reported that it replaces the earlier App Access setting and lets users choose, from one place, which apps Siri, Search and suggestions can access, including selecting several apps at once. Users can also now copy only part of a Siri response instead of the whole answer.

Siri AI gains five languages in iOS 27.2: French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese and Spanish. Cult of Mac noted that the device language has to be set to the matching language for the feature to work. The assistant requires an iPhone 15 Pro or later model, and Apple's release notes, as quoted by MacRumors, state that Siri AI is not available in the European Union or mainland China.

Other AI features arrive in the same release. Messages gains Suggested Actions, which offer shortcuts based on the conversation, such as creating a calendar event or a reminder. Photos now marks images created or edited with generative tools in Photos and Image Playground with SynthID watermarking, according to MacRumors.

Several changes are not about AI. Apple Music has new branding: Cult of Mac reported that the red icon background is replaced with white and the musical note is now black, with blue accents in the app. Apple TV gains household profiles, Podcasts splits its Home tab into New Episodes and Continue Playing, and FaceTime calls can include a third-party sign language interpreter or live captioner.

One expected feature did not ship. The redesigned Health app was removed during the beta period, so the older app remains in the public release. Beebom reported that Apple plans to release the new Health app in a separate update later in the year. Users can install iOS 27.2 from Settings, General, Software Update.

In NeuraFeed's reading, memory is the change most users will notice, because it lets Siri carry a request across days instead of treating each question as new. Apple pairs that memory with personal data such as voicemails and calendar invitations. The Excluded Apps control suggests Apple expects some users to want limits on how much of their phone the assistant reads.
The next test is reach: Siri AI still does not run in the European Union or mainland China, and Apple has not given a date for those regions in the sources reviewed here.
